items.title: Does Evolution Undermine Objective Morality? | Quayshawn Spencer
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if our moral instincts evolved to help us survive rather than discover what is right?*

Quayshawn Spencer examines how evolutionary biology challenges the foundations of moral philosophy. If natural selection shapes our moral intuitions for reproductive success rather than truth, can those intuitions still support universal moral principles?

1:01 The Evolutionary Origins of Moral Intuitions
3:32 Why Evolution Favors Moral Relativism
4:38 The Challenge of Universal Moral Standards
6:41 What Evolution Can and Cannot Tell Us About Morality

*Quayshawn Spencer* is the Robert S. Blank Presidential Associate Professor of Philosophy and Undergraduate Chair at the University of Pennsylvania.

items.title: Can Evolution Explain Consciousness and Reason? | Thomas Nagel
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Could mind and matter emerge from something more fundamental than either?*

Thomas Nagel revisits the arguments of Mind and Cosmos, questioning whether evolutionary materialism can fully explain consciousness, rationality, and objective value. He considers teleology, the limits of reductionism, and speculative alternatives in which the potential for consciousness may be built into reality itself.

0:00 Two Ways of Explaining Consciousness and Evolution
4:14 Objective Value and the Limits of Reductionism
7:16 Moral Realism and the Challenge to Darwinian Explanations
10:04 Teleology and the Possibility of Value-Driven Explanations
13:01 Intelligent Design and Philosophical Assumptions
17:04 Nagel's Atheism and His Attitude Toward God's Existence
19:08 Beyond Materialism and Theism Toward a Deeper Reality

*Thomas Nagel* is an American philosopher and Professor of Philosophy and Law at New York University. His work focuses on philosophy of mind, ethics, and political philosophy, and he is especially known for his influential critique of reductionist accounts of consciousness.

items.title: Why the Ego Wants to Believe in Reincarnation | Acharya Prashant
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:

Acharya Prashant argues that the ego can turn reincarnation into a promise of future relief, postponing the liberation that spiritual philosophy seeks in the present.

items.title: Can Logic Help Us Understand God? | Michael Murray
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Can philosophical reasoning clarify religious belief without reducing theology to logic?*

Michael Murray explains how analytic theology brings philosophical methods into conversation with traditional theology. He examines the influence of Hume and Kant, the objections raised by theologians and biblical scholars, and the challenge of balancing rigorous reasoning with the meaning conveyed through sacred texts.

0:00 Introducing Analytic Theology and Its Critics
1:04 Hume, Kant, and the Limits of Human Reason
3:49 Analytic Theology and Philosophy of Religion
4:43 The Challenge of Stories, Metaphors, and Logic
6:26 Biblical Interpretation and Philosophical Reasoning

*Michael J. Murray* is a philosopher and former Professor of Philosophy at Franklin & Marshall College who has held leadership roles at the John Templeton Foundation. His research focuses on the history of philosophy, particularly Gottfried Leibniz, and contemporary philosophy of religion, including the problem of evil, animal suffering, and the origins of religious belief.

items.title: What Are the Nine Levels of Nothing? | Robert Lawrence Kuhn, Interviewed by Àlex Gómez-Marín
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What would it take for absolutely nothing to exist?*

Robert Lawrence Kuhn traces his lifelong fascination with existence, from a frightening childhood realization to decades of conversations with philosophers and scientists. He examines competing explanations for why anything exists and explores nine levels of nothingness to ask whether even physical laws, abstract objects, and possibilities can be eliminated.

0:00 A Childhood Fear of Nothing
3:36 Competing Answers and Kinds of Necessity
7:46 Investigating Nothing Through Subtraction
10:46 Removing God, Consciousness, and Abstract Objects
12:19 Possibilities and the Ultimate Nothing

*Robert Lawrence Kuhn* is the creator, executive producer, writer, and host of _Closer To Truth,_ which has featured more than 500 leading scientists, philosophers, and creative thinkers in more than 5,000 videos and more than 350 public television episodes on PBS stations. He holds a PhD in anatomy/neuroscience from the UCLA Brain Research Institute and an MBA from MIT's Sloan School of Management. He is the author or editor of more than 30 books, including _The Mystery of Existence: Why Is There Anything At All?_ (with John Leslie), and the author of the Landscape of Consciousness, a taxonomy of more than 500 theories of consciousness.

*Àlex Gómez-Marín* is a Spanish physicist turned neuroscientist. He holds a PhD in theoretical physics and a Masters in biophysics from the University of Barcelona. He was a research fellow at the EMBL-CRG Centre for Genomic Regulation and at the Champalimaud Centre for the Unknown in Lisbon. His research spans from the origins of the arrow of time in inert systems, to the neurobiology of action-perception in living organisms such as flies, worms, mice, and humans.

He considers whether this distinction can relieve God of responsibility for evil and why such arguments may help believers understand their faith without convincing skeptics.

items.title: Why Memory May Be Essential to Consciousness | Victoria Trumbull
items.author: Closer To Truth

Victoria Trumbull revisits Augustine and Henri Bergson to explore memory as the continuity underlying mental life. She challenges the idea that remembering is simply retrieving stored information, examining how the past remains active in present experience and what this might reveal about the soul.

*Victoria Trumbull* is a philosopher, researcher, and writer whose work concerns the nature of the mind and the relationship between time, memory, and the soul. She received her DPhil from the University of Oxford and is the author of _On the Memory of the Soul: Augustine and Bergson’s Metaphysics._

Stuart Kauffman proposes that life arises through catalytic and construction closure, where molecular networks help produce their own components. *Stuart Kauffman* is an American theoretical biologist, complex systems researcher, and Professor Emeritus of Biochemistry at the University of Pennsylvania. His research focuses on the origin of life, self-organization, and biological complexity, exploring how complex living systems emerge through processes beyond Darwinian natural selection.

items.title: Is Art Just Cheesecake for the Mind? | Pascal Boyer
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Could our enjoyment of art be an evolutionary byproduct, or does it serve a useful purpose?*

Pascal Boyer explores how neuroscience, cultural comparisons, and evolutionary psychology might help explain aesthetic experience. He contrasts the idea of art as a pleasurable byproduct with the possibility that artistic activities train cognitive abilities, while emphasizing that neither hypothesis has yet received substantial research support.

0:00 Aesthetic Experience and Artists as Tricksters
2:08 Art as Cheesecake or Training for the Mind
4:36 The Loose Connection to Theology

*Pascal Boyer* is a cognitive anthropologist and evolutionary psychologist, and Professor of Sociocultural Anthropology and Psychology at Washington University in St. Louis. His research explores the cognitive and evolutionary foundations of religious belief, examining how human mental processes shape cultural traditions and concepts of supernatural beings.

items.title: Can Morality Be Binding Without Objective Justification? | Michael Ruse
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Why do moral obligations feel absolute if they emerged through evolution?*

Michael Ruse explains how cooperation, reciprocal altruism, and kin selection may have shaped human morality. He then explores why moral obligations can remain deeply binding even if their authority comes from evolved psychology rather than an independent moral reality.

0:00 Altruism as a Biological Adaptation
2:07 Reciprocal Altruism, Kin Selection, and Their Limits 
5:40 Moral Obligations and Prescriptive Ethics 
6:59 Metaethics and Morality as an Adaptation 
9:21 Absolute Morality Without Objective Foundations

*Michael Ruse* (1940–2024) was a leading philosopher of biology known for his foundational work on evolutionary theory, ethics, the creation–evolution controversy, and the relationship between science and religion.
